keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 80,928 km2: Latvia of 1940 to 1943 with the Abrene (Pytalovo) district, a part of which ("about 2% of Latvia's territory") was ceded to the RSFSR in 1944. Cliopatria's Republic of Latvia of 1939 is 67,865 km2 and has no shape for 1940-1991; the Soviet years lie inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes.
New keyframe, 79,411 km2 against the infobox 64,589 km2 for 1989 (ratio 0.81; the gazetteer overcounts Latvia): Latvia without the Abrene district strip ceded to the RSFSR in 1944.

sources.title: Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: Occupation 17 June 1940; SSR established 21 July 1940; annexation 5 August 1940; Riga occupied 1 July 1941; 1944 Abrene cession (about 2%); sovereignty 28 July 1989; independence restored 4 May 1990 and 21 August 1991; area 64,589 km2 (1989); capital Riga; silent on renaming.

notes: No Cliopatria row for 1940-1991 (Cliopatria's Republic of Latvia is 1920-1939 and 1992 on); the Soviet years lie inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. The page does not give the Pytalovo area or name Pytalovo, and does not rename the republic; the Abrene circle (20 km, 1,770 km2 against about 2% of 64,589 km2 = 1,290 km2) is the researcher's. Date mismatch: the Latvian page puts the cession in 1944, the Estonian page puts the Petseri annexation in 1945. The end of the occupation is 1945 on the infobox and "1944" in the text. Counterparts: republic-of-latvia exists (Cliopatria); nazi-germany is a Cliopatria polity.
